business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa — International Company (IC) regime under the International Companies Act 1987
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law heritage with local statutory enactments and customary land-holding principles)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreement between the Independent State of Samoa and Australia (in force)
Double Taxation Arrangement between the Independent State of Samoa and New Zealand (in force)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus; signed 14 June 2017, in force 13 December 2020)
South Pacific Regional Trade and Economic Cooperation Agreement (SPARTECA; Australia and New Zealand preferential access)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended, including the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Acts 2013 and 2018); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2012; Companies Act 2001; International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019; and the AML/CFT directives and supervisory guidelines of the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, and the Central Bank of Samoa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport-issuing authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin, or consular legalization by the Samoan diplomatic/consular post where the origin country is not party to the 1961 Apostille Convention

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 4 (incorporation), 6 (application), 8 (share capital), 14 (registered office), 17 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form 1) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no statutory escrow or bank deposit precondition. Shares may be denominated in any currency, par or no par, and issued for such consideration as the board determines.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers named in the Application for Incorporation be and are hereby confirmed as the first shareholders of the Company and that the issued share capital set out in the Register of Members be approved. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the address of the licensed resident agent and that the resident agent is authorised to maintain all statutory records. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] be appointed Company Secretary, each with full authority to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts and direct the day-to-day executive search and headhunting business. RESOLVED that the Board adopts the Articles as its constitution and approves any subsequent filing required under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the international company name and obtain name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) – Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request in writing or through the licensed resident agent, specifying the proposed name and intended ISIC 7830 executive search business. The Registrar will check for similarity with existing entities, restricted words, and required suffixes such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd'.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport of each subscriber/director
Certified proof of residential address of each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or reserved subject to conditions, the applicant may amend the proposed name and resubmit; an administrative review request can be lodged with the Registrar within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare memorandum and articles of association and shareholder consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed resident agent on behalf of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, describing the company's object as executive search, headhunting and talent acquisition services. Include authorised share capital, share classes, director powers, and indemnity provisions. The subscriber(s) must sign the memorandum in the presence of the resident agent or a notary public.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the constitutional documents for non-compliance with International Companies Act 1987, the resident agent will revise and file an amended set with the Registrar's observations addressed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation application and constitutional documents with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the licensed resident agent, submit the executed Application for Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, and statutory declarations to SIFSA. The application must state that the registered office will be maintained by a licensed resident agent in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of resident agent to act
Statutory declaration of compliance by a subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is defective, SIFSA issues a requisition notice specifying deficiencies; the applicant has 21 days to cure, after which the application lapses unless extended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay the statutory filing fee and receive the certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official filing fee together with any government stamp duty via bank transfer to the SIFSA authorised account. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation dated the day of registration and publish the incorporation in the official registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where payment is applied incorrectly, the applicant must provide proof of transfer and request a re-allocation; if the Certificate contains errors, a correction request under section 132 of the International Companies Act may be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a physical or virtual board meeting. Approve the issuance of shares to the founding shareholders, adopt the registered office address and resident agent appointment, elect the Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary, and approve the banking signatories for the retainer fee and Wise B2B payment rails.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director is unavailable, a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting may be executed and circulated; if a conflict of interest is detected, the conflicted director must recuse and the resolution must be documented accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint a licensed resident agent and establish the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a resident agency agreement with a SIFSA-licensed agent who will maintain the registered office in Samoa, keep the statutory registers, and act as the point of service for legal process. File the Notice of Registered Office and Resident Agent with the Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent resigns or is removed, a new licensed agent must be appointed within 21 days and the change filed with the Registrar; failure may lead to administrative strike-off, which can be reversed by filing late notices and paying late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the domestic business licence required for executive search operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business and Trade Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The International Company must obtain a Business Licence to lawfully transact with local employers or maintain a physical office in Samoa. Submit the completed application, the Certificate of Incorporation, and proof of registered office to MCIL, and pay the annual licence fee assessed against the declared business category for personnel placement services.
required_dossiers: Valid ID of the principal officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, the company may appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 14 days; resubmission with a clarified scope of services and updated zoning approval will be accepted if the refusal was due to documentation gaps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-incorporation registrations for employment, tax, and banking operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Samoa National Provident Fund, and Accrual Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Samoa International Company for any domestic obligations if it employs local staff, including taxpayer identification, national provident fund registration, and accident compensation. Open a corporate operating bank account for wire retainers and enable Wise B2B treasury settlements for international invoices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, the company may submit a nil return or declaration of non-activity to the Ministry of Revenue; for bank account rejection, alternative licensed banks may be approached with the same incorporation package.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business and Trade Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998 (personnel placement and employment agency services)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environment Protection Agency (SEPA) within the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration not required for office-based executive search services; activity is classified as 'permitted' under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004, Schedule 1, insofar as it involves no industrial processes, manufacturing, or hazardous materials
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or VOC point-source emissions. Domestic sewage from office washrooms and kitchenettes must comply with the Water Resources Management Act 2008 (COD/BOD discharge limits applicable to municipal septic or sewer systems). Solid waste must be collected by a licensed waste carrier and disposed at the Tafaigata landfill. Waste electrical or electronic equipment must be handled per the Waste Management Act 2001. No air emission abatement equipment is required for a non-industrial office operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); building occupancy approval from the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA); and workplace health and safety clearance confirming compliance with the Labour and Employment Act 2013, including adequate lighting, sanitation, first aid provisions, and emergency egress for office staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), Apia, Samoa; official online portal and e-Services platform at https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Samoa International Company (IC) engaged in executive search and headhunting: (1) appoint a licensed registered agent in Samoa pursuant to the International Companies Act 2007; (2) file the memorandum and articles of association with the Registrar of International Companies, pay the applicable incorporation fee, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; (3) upon incorporation, the registered agent submits the IC particulars via the Ministry of Revenue e-Services portal to obtain the company Tax Identification Number (TIN), which is the single statutory identifier for tax correspondence and, if required, VAGST registration; (4) because the IC's offshore business falls within the tax-exempt zone, no income tax registration return is required and the IC instead maintains its annual government licence fee; (5) if the IC makes any taxable supply in Samoa, the same TIN is used for the VAGST application and separate VAT ID is not issued. A board resolution authorising the agent and a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation are retained in the statutory records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a US-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election. The IC is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax by operation of the International Companies Act 2007; therefore no entity classification election is necessary. A registered agent may elect voluntary VAGST registration under the VAGST Act 2005 for an otherwise exempt offshore IC in order to recover input VAGST on local administrative expenses, subject to Ministry of Revenue approval. An IC may also elect to redomicile, continue, or convert to an ordinary Samoan company where it ceases to meet the offshore exemption conditions; such an election triggers ordinary resident company taxation and must be filed through the Ministry of Revenue.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Samoa: Value Added Goods and Services Tax, VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 75,000 (Samoan Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Currency ISO code: WST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has no mandatory real-time e-invoicing, no government fiscal clearance platform, and no digital stamping requirement. VAGST-registered suppliers may issue paper or electronic tax invoices; the Ministry of Revenue requires only that invoices contain the prescribed particulars under the VAGST Act 2005 and that returns and TIN applications are filed electronically through the Ministry's online e-Services portal. API integration with the tax authority is optional and not a precondition for claiming output tax credit or zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying supplies of services are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2005. For executive search and headhunting services rendered by a Samoa IC to offshore corporate clients, the IC may apply the 0% rate only where: (a) the recipient of the supply is a non-resident not physically present in Samoa at the time of supply; (b) the headhunting service is not performed by way of on-shore secondment or executive placement within Samoa's domestic labour market; (c) the CV sourcing, candidate interviewing, market research, and negotiation support are conducted offshore or through offshore communication channels; (d) the rights and economic benefits of the supply are enjoyed outside Samoa; and (e) the IC holds contemporaneous documentary evidence of the offshore supply chain. Because the IC operates within Samoa's offshore tax-exempt zone and is excluded from Samoan exchange control rules, retention and success-fee payments may be received in any freely convertible currency into the IC's offshore account without Central Bank of Samoa approval; no mandatory conversion of foreign currency into Samoan Tala is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed executive search or headhunting retainer agreement naming the non-resident corporate client and the offshore roles covered
Detailed VAGST tax invoice and statement of account showing the supply as an export of services and applying the 0% rate
Evidence of cross-border fee settlement, including SWIFT MT103 payment message or Wise B2B transaction record, matching the invoiced retainer and success fee
Substantiation of offshore place of supply and place of use, including interview locations, video-meeting records, candidate database access logs, and offshore email or correspondence files

Internal zero-rated supplies schedule reconciling the VAGST return to underlying contracts and remittance evidence; a physical customs export declaration is not applicable to intangible headhunting services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue may audit any zero-rated export supply and require the entire zero-rating substantiation bundle to be produced on demand. Where export zero-rating is disallowed due to missing non-resident evidence, the VAT output tax becomes immediately recoverable with the zero-rated input credits clawed back plus default interest. Fraudulent zero-rating, false invoices, or deliberate mis-statement of the place of supply attract civil shortfall penalties of up to 100% of the evaded tax, increased to 200% for a second or deliberate offence, monetary fines of up to WST 50,000 per offence, and imprisonment for up to three years under the Tax Administration Act 2015 and the VAGST Act 2005. The Commissioner may also issue retrospective assessments outside the ordinary limitation period where evasion is established and may issue a direction freezing retainer, success-fee, or commission assets held on behalf of the IC to secure the clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; exchange control powers delegated under the Exchange Control Act 1978 and Exchange Control Regulations 1984 (Samoa). The International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) expressly disapplies most exchange-control approval requirements for International Companies, substituting a lighter compliance reporting regime where funds are channelled through onshore Samoan banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a CBS-managed float; current-account transactions (cross-border service fees, executive-search retainers) are freely convertible subject to documentary verification by the instructing local bank. Capital-account transactions (share capital injections, dividend repatriations) by an International Company are exempt from prior CBS approval under the ICA 1987, provided the transaction is recorded on CBS Form ECM/ICA disclosures; profit remittance is reportedly tax-free given the IC zero-tax status, but an onshore correspondent bank may impose an enhanced EDD review on high-value WST/foreign-currency conversions. Repatriation of non-resident IC earnings is structurally liberalized, yet banks routinely require an IC certificate of status plus a certificate from the registered agent confirming the beneficial owners are non-residents of Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa does not impose a statutorily binding surrender requirement on service exporters; the Exchange Control Regulations require repatriation of export proceeds to a licensed Samoan bank within 180 days from invoice date, failing which the accumulated shortfall must be surrendered to a commercial bank at the prevailing exchange rate. For International Companies, the Central Bank exempts proceeds routed to an offshore IC account held in a foreign currency; when such proceeds are brought onshore, the bank will enforce a 100% monetization upon conversion consistent with general surrender practice. Executive-search retainers and placement fees should be evidenced via signed client engagement agreements and dated invoices to avoid adverse classification as undeclared capital receipts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_license_interaction: Executive search and headhunting services are non-financial and do not require a CBS financial-services license; the IC must, however, maintain a valid business license issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and ensure the ISIC 7830 activity is recorded on the SIFA register, as SIFA coordinates with CBS on cross-border payment monitoring (the operational 'license gate' for opening corporate accounts and performing cross-border wires is SIFA active status).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.anti_money_laundering_integration: CBS AML/CFT Guidelines (rev. 2023, implementing the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018 and FIU framework) classify executive-search and professional services as a 'Designated Non-Financial Business and Profession' activity only at the company-client advisory stage; pure headhunting with retainer payments is treated as low-risk, but Samoan banks will apply a risk-based approach to IC clients and file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit for anomalies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.statutory_deadline_and_filing_integratio: The IC's annual SIFA renewal (calendar-year window) must be settled prior to any major cross-border disbursement in Q1 of each year; banks automatically cross-reference SIFA active status, and a lapsed SIFA license is an immediate block on outbound wire processing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited (BSP) – Samoa Branch (Apia)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (WST/USD/AUD) + Foreign Currency Sweep
Operational WST/USD Account with dedicated relationship manager for offshore corporate clients
Operational WST Account with Telegraphic Transfer and Foreign Exchange Desk
Operational WST Account (minimum balance WST 25,000; stricter IC risk appetite)
Operational WST/USD Account (limited digital infrastructure; slower wire turnaround)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: CONDITIONAL / LOW for primary treasury rails. Wise (TransferWise) B2B is legally usable only as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail for low-value retainer receipts (e.g., sub-USD 10,000 from headhunted clients) and employee expense reimbursements; it is not a licensed depository institution in Samoa and cannot settle payroll into Samoan bank accounts directly. Samoan FX control does not recognize EMIs as acceptance-parties for mandatory export-proceeds repatriation; therefore Wise balances must be regularly swept to a licensed Samoan commercial bank to preserve IC compliance status. The Central Bank of Samoa has no EMI license class; any persistent routing of large retainers through offshore EMIs without a local bank intermediary would be deemed a capital-account circumvention.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted at all tier1 Samoan banks for ICs, subject to bank-board-approved digital KYC procedures; banks require: (1) a live video verification call with each signatory; (2) certified copies of passports endorsed by a notary or Samoan consular officer; (3) an introducing certificate from a SIFA-licensed registered agent; (4) evidence of the IC's Samoa registered office address. A physical visit to Apia is not mandatorily required for standard low-risk ICs, but a physical presence becomes effectively mandatory if the bank's AML committee flags the high-risk jurisdiction, trade-line mismatch, or beneficial-owner links to high-risk geographies; additional board-approval will be required for such cases with a 4–8 week timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with nominee/registered-agent directors and no commercial substance in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Incorporation; registered agent's statutory declaration confirming UBO register maintenance; detailed group structure chart; management agreements or contractual revenue contracts from overseas clients; audited or reviewed management accounts; IC tax-exempt certificate from Samoa Ministry of Revenue; operational substance report listing the Apia registered office and any outsourced administration services; client retainer agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity mismatch between 'Executive Search/Headhunting' and bank's expected pattern (high withdrawal velocity, payroll to foreign nationals, crypto-adjacent clients)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 7830 trade classification letter from the Ministry of Commerce; professional indemnity insurance policy; employee/contractor list with passport copies; payroll schedule; placement contracts; sample fee invoices; a written narrative of the end-to-end business flow (client onboarding to placement fee receipt).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failed or inconsistent source-of-funds evidence for initial capital injection into the Samoan bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified bank statements of the transferring entity for 6–12 months; signed capital contribution resolution; shareholder register; UBO source-of-wealth declaration with independent evidence (property valuations, sale contracts, inheritance documents, dividends); confirmation from solicitor/accountant of the transferring jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Samoan IC receives payments from multiple related offshore entities in quick succession, triggering structuring query
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany master agreement; client-vendor matrix; retainer commission schedule; transactions-log narrative; dual-entity consolidation summary demonstrating that each inbound wire maps to a distinct named client engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment rail 'Wise B2B' flagged as a potential money-service-business (MSB) or unlicensed virtual-asset service provider when the bank screens the counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Wise Business account activation certificate and license in the origination jurisdiction; explanation of Wise as an auxiliary rail only; demonstration that the Wise account is in the IC's verified name; a standing instruction to sweep balances to the Samoan bank within 5 business days; review of Samoa FIU guidance on physical-vs-electronic transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions-list hits on the beneficial owner, director, or client-company counterparty involved in technology recruitment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-media screening report from an independent provider (World-Check or Dow Jones); explanation memo for any name-match; sanctions self-certification; legal opinion from an international law firm confirming no ownership by blocked persons; waiver or enhanced due diligence approval from the bank's compliance committee.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.onboarding_timeline_and_prerequisites: Standard IC onboarding at tier1 banks completes in 10–15 business days assuming a SIFA-licensed registered agent, clean beneficial ownership, and complete evidence; enhanced EDD cases extend to 30–60 business days; pre-validation of one bank relationship at BSP and one at Bank of Samoa in parallel is recommended to maintain operational resilience. A signed SIFA 'Certificate of Good Standing' is a non-negotiable prerequisite at all tier1 Samoan banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.bank_account_structure_standard: Recommended structure: one multi-currency USD/WST operational account at the primary bank, one discreet WST corporate savings account for surplus reserve; all client invoices invoiced in USD with WST conversion executed at mid-market through the corporate FX desk; a separate retainer-collection account at Bank of Samoa may be maintained where Chinese-speaking traditional-family clients remit via Wise B2B.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire routing: originating bank transmits SWIFT MT103 to the Samoan beneficiary bank; beneficiary bank credits the IC operational account. The remitter must state in Field 70 the purpose code 'Capital Injection / Shareholder Loan' with a supporting purpose narrative; CBS regulation requires the beneficiary bank to obtain a certified copy of the IC shareholder resolution and register of members before effecting credit. Where funds originate from greater-China family trusts or the mainland, the remitter should add a remittance remark matching the China SAFE 'other investment/capital' category; no separate CBS pre-approval is required for the IC, but the bank will file a CBS exchange-control report. For retained service-fee revenue (retainers), Field 70 must read 'Service fees – executive search retainer' plus the client engagement number; clean same-day clearing is achieved if funds arrive before the bank's wire cut-off (12:00 noon Apia time) and are not at-risk of OFAC/sanctions screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Executive search disbursements (post-placement bonuses, contractor payroll, referral incentives) settle via SWIFT MT103 from the Samoan IC's account to the beneficiary's bank; Field 71A 'OUR' cost arrangement is recommended for executive candidates' cross-border tips; internet-banking-initiated wires over WST 50,000 require a redundant FM-check by the bank's foreign-exchange desk. For disbursements to subcontractor headhunters in tier-1 global hubs, a SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover may be triggered when the beneficiary bank instructs an intermediary; the IC must store the invoice plus placement agreement for five years. Commercial letters of credit (documentary LCs) are not practical for professional service payments, but the bank can issue a standby LC to a client-side procurement portal on request; the cost for a WST 250,000 standby LC is approximately 0.75–1.2% p.a. payable in advance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards (up to 12 months tenor) with licensed Samoan commercial banks for USD-WST conversion of retainer pipelines based on invoiced and un-invoiced committed receivables; CBS notification required above WST 1 million notional.

FX options (European-style, medium-tenor) purchased outright (no premium-selling) for USD-WST protecting against sharp tala depreciation in periods of fiscal stress; requires a signed risk-acknowledgement letter with the bank.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) only to swap USD fixed-rate receivables into WST-linked exposures if the IC maintains debt in Samoan banks; requires prior CBS regulatory consent; the IC's zero-tax status means hedging gains are not taxable.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in WST are not commonly supported by local Samoan banks; if the bank's offshore parent operator offers NDFs, they are permissible only when the ultimate settlement is in USD against the WST fix, subject to a bona-fide commercial hedge test and CBS reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_buffer_and_reserve_policy: Maintain a minimum operating buffer of WST 120,000 (approximately 2 months operating expenses) in the local operational account; surplus WST balances above buffer are converted to USD via delivered forward layers of 3/6/9/12 months to fund subsequent offshore operational disbursements; target intra-day cash at a level so that no outbound wire exceeds 40% of the account balance without same-day liquidity cover.

payment_rails_priority_matrix.rail: SWIFT MT103 via BSP/BoS local account
payment_rails_priority_matrix.use_case: Retainer receipts from corporate clients over USD 10k; payroll; settlement of tax-free dividend to non-resident shareholders
Small retainer receipts and client refunds under USD 10k; non-Samoan contractor disbursements
Liquidity for a client-side procurement portal or headhunter-level outsourcing guarantee

payment_rails_priority_matrix.rail: Telegraphic Transfer via Samoa Commercial Bank
payment_rails_priority_matrix.use_case: Domestic WST settlement with Samoan payroll/executive candidates

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.reporting_and_exchange_control_calendar: Exchange-control report to CBS is submitted monthly by the local commercial bank on behalf of the IC (the bank aggregates transaction flows); the IC should independently file a shadow internal reconciliation monthly; annual SIFA renewal before 1 March; any annual cross-border dividend remittance exceeding WST 200,000 should be notified to the bank 10 business days in advance to permit CBS reporting and potential deferred capital-account review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) for Samoa International Company, containing registered name, registration number, registered office, registered agent, director particulars, issued share capital and beneficial ownership confirmation schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) calendar month (30 days) after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the filing cycle is anniversary-based, not calendar-year-based, with the first annual return due 30 days after the first incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a recurring penalty of approximately WST 100 (USD 37) per commenced month of default under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations; if default continues for three months or more, the Registrar serves a written default notice and may publish a strike-off notice in the Savali official gazette; after a 30-day objection period the company is struck off the International Companies Register, and the company and each officer in default remain exposed to statutory fines and disqualification, with restoration available only by Court order or Registrar consent upon payment of all arrears, penalties and restoration fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Renewal Fee Payment (Government License / Annual Retention Fee to maintain active status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Revenue Collection Account, Ministry of Finance, Samoa International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable no later than the same 30-day anniversary window as the Annual Return; the renewal payment is processed concurrently with the Annual Return submission to prevent a lapse in the company's active and in-good-standing status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment by the anniversary due date triggers an automatic late surcharge of approximately 10% of the annual tariff; continued non-payment for 90 days entitles the Registrar to dissolve the company administratively without a Court order; dissolution divests the company's assets in favour of the State and appears on the public register as 'struck off', with restoration permitted only on full settlement of outstanding fees, surcharges, penalties and legal costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership / AML/CFT Client Due Diligence Confirmation (retained by the SIFA-licensed registered agent as the company's statutory record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (retained on file); subject to lawful on-site inspection and supervisory review by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Refreshed and documented within the 30-day anniversary period in parallel with the Annual Return; additionally triggered within 14 days after any share transfer, allotment, or change of beneficial owner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government fee applies; however, failure of the registered agent to maintain current UBO confirmation breaches the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 and SIFA AML/CFT Rules, exposing the agent to supervisory fines of up to WST 1,000 (USD 370) per contravention and possible revocation of the agent's license, which would force the company to engage a replacement licensed agent or be struck off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company engaged purely in cross-border executive search and headhunting is exempt from the statutory independent audit requirement; a mandatory audit is triggered only if (a) the company holds a licensed activity under the International Banking Act, the International Insurance Act, or the Trustee Companies Act; (b) the Registrar or the Minister of Commerce issues a formal direction to audit due to suspected irregularity; or (c) the company's Articles, a lender, or an investor expressly require an audit. Non-resident headhunting fee income does not create a domestic audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting records must disclose the company's financial position with reasonable accuracy in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987; financial statements, when prepared under a statutory or contractual trigger, must be prepared using IFRS as adopted in Samoa or the applicable local GAAP recognised by the Samoan Institute of Accountants; the company is not required to file or publicly deposit financial statements with the International Companies Registry, but the records must be sufficient to reconstruct a true and fair view of the company's affairs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The sole or corporate director of the International Company must deliver to the SIFA-licensed registered agent a signed written confirmation at each annual anniversary stating that the beneficial ownership schedule and shareholding structure on file remain accurate, or attaching a revised UBO schedule in the form prescribed by the AML/CFT Rules; every share transfer or change of beneficial ownership occurring during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the Annual Return; no public UBO filing is made to the government registry, and the confidential UBO file maintained by the registered agent is disclosed only to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) including transfers, allotments and beneficial ownership details
Register of Directors and of the company secretary
Register of Charges and share security interests
Minute Book of directors' resolutions and shareholders' resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 900 per annum (representative low-risk executive-search vehicle: approximately USD 650)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory for a non-licensed headhunting International Company; voluntary certified audit by a Samoan-licensed or New Zealand-affiliated practitioner typically USD 2,000 – USD 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (ordinary resident Samoa companies); effective 0% for International Companies exempt under the International Companies Act 1987
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies enjoy a statutory full exemption from Samoa corporate income tax on world income, exemption from dividend distribution tax, exemption from capital gains recognition, and no payroll or social contribution levy on foreign-source executive search fees; no general tax holidays apply to domestic resident companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Income Tax Return for Companies (Ministry of Revenue Form CIT-100) filed via the Ministry of Revenue Online Services portal (www.revenue.gov.ws); International Companies file the International Company Annual Return and Economic Substance Declaration via the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Resident companies: filing due within 6 months after the accounting year-end, with provisional tax installments due quarterly; exempt International Companies: annual government fee and substance declaration due within 1 month of the incorporation anniversary

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income from worldwide operations (headhunting retainers, placement fees, success fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt International Company: enter 'N/A – exempt under International Companies Act 1987'; zero-rated filing via the SIFA annual return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (salaries of Samoan staff, office rent, telecommunications, professional indemnity insurance)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to a tax-exempt International Company; no deduction schedule required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after loss carryforward and concessionary deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave zero for exempt International Company
Enter '0' for International Company; attach the exemption certificate or confirmation letter issued by the Ministry of Revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Company annual government fee and economic substance attestation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the SIFA Annual Return, confirm registered agent, Samoa registered office, and physical substance indicators

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the assessed tax, default interest at 1% per month or part-month on unpaid tax, fixed daily surcharges accumulate until compliance; exempt International Companies that fail the annual fee or substance declaration incur a 10% late fee, potential reinstatement charges, and strike-off from the International Companies Register.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends paid by ordinary resident Samoa companies to non-residents; 0% for dividends and distributions paid by an exempt International Company
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a limited DTA network (notably the Samoa-China DTA). To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must submit a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) with the prescribed withholding tax treaty claim form to the Ministry of Revenue prior to payment; for an International Company, a TRC is generally not issued because the IC is statutorily exempt, and the counterparty instead accepts an Exemption Affidavit plus a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of International Companies as substantive relief documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory, typically reduced to 10% or exempt under applicable DTA; interest: 15% statutory, reduced to 0-10% under DTA; International Companies are generally outside the Samoa withholding tax net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No codified Samoa Local File/Master File statutory threshold; revenue practice benchmark is SAT 2,000,000 of cross-border related-party turnover for resident taxpayers; tax-exempt International Companies have no transfer pricing documentation obligation
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations require International Companies to demonstrate economic substance proportionate to their activities: a physical office or registered agent in Samoa, adequate employees and qualifying expenditure in Samoa, board meetings held with quorum in Samoa, and annual substance reporting; failure to meet the doctrine results in financial penalties, strike-off, and potential retrospective taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Samoan International Company as a pure invoice conduit with no physical presence while funneling executive search retainers and placement fees offshore to avoid the tax of the real revenue jurisdiction; backdating or fabricating invoices; filing false exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to 200% of the understated tax plus default interest; criminal prosecution under the Samoa Tax Administration Act exposing fines up to SAT 200,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; the exemption is void and tax is assessed at 27% with penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may have the corporate veil pierced for fraudulent conduct; personal civil restitution of evaded tax, travel bans for unpaid assessments, asset restraint orders, and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee-only directorship, no Samoa-registered office or local management, no substance return filed, zero local payroll, and no board minutes evidencing decision-making in Samoa for the headhunting agency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines for non-compliance with the Economic Substance Regulations, late fee penalties, deregistration and strike-off of the International Company, plus disqualification of the registered agent; reinstatement may be refused indefinitely.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid government fees and penalties; they face a bar from acting as directors in Samoa-controlled vehicles and adverse international reputational listings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting retainer wires and Wise Business payments without customer due diligence (KYC), concealing beneficial owners behind nominee shares, or routing candidate placement fees from sanctions-flagged jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to SAT 1,000,000 per breach under the Samoa AML/CFT framework; suspension or revocation of the trust and company service provider license; seizure and civil forfeiture of the fee proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior directors and compliance officers are individually prosecutable; money laundering convictions carry imprisonment up to 14 years, personal fines, and mandatory permanent travel bans when the offense involves cross-border wire transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting C-suite executive search and specialist technology headhunting without the required statutory business license, or misrepresenting candidate credentials to facilitate immigration or visa fraud for placed executives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate business license revocation, cease-and-desist orders from the Labour and Commerce authorities, administrative fines per unlicensed transaction, and forced refund of client retainers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution of all collected fees, exclusion from re-licensing, criminal fraud conviction with custodial sentence, and asset freezing pending investigation.
